clue.text: Erratic of USA to produce such a weapon?

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words are worked up to produce something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Erratic American policy might lead to the making of a certain missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erratic' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder: all twelve letters of ERRATIC OF USA are rearranged, with 'to produce' signalling the reworking.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile launched from the ground at aircraft is the weapon described.

clue.text: Government agents in established piece

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the word for established

parts.note: established, as in fixed, means set
G-men is US slang for FBI agents, short for government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents are planted within an established part of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or portion of a whole, a synonym for piece.

clue.text: He introduced Virginia to Elizabeth

parts.note: the Elizabethan courtier who named the American colony after the Virgin Queen and presented it, and its tobacco, to her court

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a social introduction between two women; in fact Virginia is the colony named in honour of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter, the Elizabethan explorer, sponsored the colony named Virginia in honour of the queen.

clue.text: Old scientist who converted St Michael

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the saint's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist of old who turned the saint into a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests religious conversion, fitting a saint, but it signals the anagram of ST MICHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists were medieval precursors of chemists, seeking to turn base metal into gold.

clue.text: Remarkably wide, for example

definitions.meaning: used as an adverb, ... means unusually or exceptionally, as in ... careful
in cricket a wide is one kind of run not scored off the bat, along with byes and no-balls

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, which gives a penalty run to the batting side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an intensifier meaning exceptionally, and as cricket's term for a bonus run such as a wide.

clue.text: No friend in the east would like a certain stone

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
a pal is a friend
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A loner out east might resemble a particular gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline describes something milky and iridescent, resembling the gem opal.

clue.text: Brave army leader in a state

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, historically called an Indian

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letter of army is A

explanation.surface: A courageous commander serving in one of the US states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' reads as an adjective but is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Tracked vehicles turning into coppers, possibly?

definitions.meaning: machines running on continuous tracks rather than wheels, named after a brand of crawler tractor
larvae that metamorphose into butterflies, the copper being one kind of butterfly

explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but the small copper is a butterfly, which a larva turns into.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawler tractors and tanks run on belts called this, and the larvae of butterflies such as the copper bear the same name.

clue.text: Pure ingredient of blancmange licensed

indicators.note: ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wholesome component of a dessert that has been officially approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means innocent and virtuous, like an angel.

clue.text: Only white rulers in this office?

definitions.text: Only white rulers in this office?

parts.words: Only white rulers in this office?
parts.note: the position held by the emperors of Russia, whose loyalist supporters in the civil war were known as the Whites

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a remark about race; the Whites were the anti-Bolshevik side in the Russian Civil War, loyal to the old imperial order.
explanation.definitionFit: The office and domain of a tsar, the Russian emperor whose cause the White armies fought for.

clue.text: Troubled, guilty lawman is in the soup

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the two following words are stirred up

explanation.surface: A lawman with a guilty conscience finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' is an idiom for in trouble, but here it is literal: the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spiced curry-flavoured soup of Anglo-Indian origin.

clue.text: Recluse has English clock put back with key

indicators.note: put back means the word for clock is reversed

parts.note: a timer is a clock
E is one of the musical keys, A to G

explanation.surface: A hermit with an English clock moves it back and adds a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the clock word; 'key' is a musical key, here E, one of the notes A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit living in solitude.

clue.text: An enormous trouble for a lady's maid

parts.note: an becomes A, the indefinite article
big means enormous
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A domestic servant who causes her mistress endless bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail became a generic name for a lady's maid after a waiting-woman in a 17th-century play.

clue.text: Reinforce small strike in sympathy with church leaders

parts.note: a pat is a light tap, as on the back to console someone
CH, the standard abbreviation for church, is also its leading pair of letters

explanation.surface: Workers stage a small walkout supporting senior clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike in sympathy' suggests industrial action, but it is a consoling pat.
explanation.definitionFit: To patch something is to mend or strengthen it with an extra piece.

clue.text: Primaries brought out such showmen

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters of primaries are drawn out into a new order

explanation.surface: Election primaries produce flamboyant promoters.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios, plural impresari, are producers and managers of shows and concerts.

clue.text: Split crest of bird given at Christmas

parts.note: to part is to split
a ridge is a crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A split crest belonging to a festive gift bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A game bird famous from the carol in which one is given in a pear tree.

clue.text: Derelict ancestral house

indicators.note: derelict means ruined, so the letters of the next word are in disorder

explanation.surface: A dilapidated family home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a building, but here it is a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty of three English kings, rivals of York in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Barking man is Hazel's protector

definitions.meaning: barking is British slang for mad, so a crazy fellow
the woody shell enclosing the kernel of a hazel nut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name; it is the tree whose nut has a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a crazy person, and literally the hard shell guarding a hazel's kernel.

clue.text: AI means of recollection? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: AI means of recollection? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: quite the opposite signals the letters of the first two words turned round into a different order

explanation.surface: Artificial intelligence as a memory aid is ridiculed as its very reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AI MEANS are rearranged; and the whole clue says the word means the opposite of a way of remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the opposite of a means of recalling things.

clue.text: Everyone in California finds the arum-lily

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody in California discovers a particular flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Calla is the genus name commonly given to the arum lily.

clue.text: Body of senior politicians with its back to the wall

definitions.meaning: the group of top ministers who run a government

definitions.text: with its back to the wall
definitions.meaning: a cupboard of furniture, which normally stands against a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'back to the wall' suggests a government in crisis, but a piece of furniture literally stands that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministers heading a government, and a cupboard with shelves that stands against a wall.

clue.text: Tailless alley-cat possibly like milk?

indicators.note: possibly means the remaining letters could be arranged another way
tailless says the end of the word alley loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stray cat without a tail might seem milky?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' cuts the Y from the end of 'alley', leaving ALLECAT; 'possibly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal means relating to or resembling milk, from Latin lac.

clue.text: Feeler put out by social worker to retired girl

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, and a worker ant

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, so the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A social worker sends out a feeler to a girl who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a job, but it is an ant; 'retired' turns ANNE into ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's sensory feeler.

clue.text: A great stop at sea

parts.note: vast means great in size

explanation.surface: A big halt on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a sailors' command meaning stop or hold.

clue.text: Novel old instrument with two keys

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval stringed instrument played with a bow
C is a musical key
A is another musical key

explanation.surface: An antique instrument fitted with a couple of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the Daphne du Maurier book.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's famous 1938 book bears this title.

clue.text: Port in Wales was switched to North Sea

indicators.note: switched means the three letters of was change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Welsh harbour was moved to the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city and port in south Wales.

clue.text: Room in gaol for Brown, gone wrong?

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: gone wrong means the word gone is scrambled

explanation.surface: A cell for Brown, whose plans have gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads as a surname; it is the colour dun.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell, as in a castle.

clue.text: Concerned with a branch of learning, go mad!

definitions.text: Concerned with a branch of learning

parts.note: to depart is to go
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: An academic is urged to go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Departmental relates to a department, a division of a university or school.
